Trial.Public_title: Effect of Physical Exercise training on the level of body function, intensity of Back Pain, Depressive Symptoms and Ability to Breathe in Chronic Kidney Patients undergoing hemodialysis
Trial.Scientific_title: Effectiveness of Physical Exercise training on the level of functionality, intensity of Low Back Pain, Depressive Symptoms and Respiratory Capacity in Chronic Kidney Patients undergoing hemodialysis
Trial.Primary_sponsor: Faculdade Ciências Médicas de Minas Gerais
Trial.Study_design: a phase n/a, non-randomized-controlled, open, other, treatment
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Faculdade Ciências Médicas de Minas Gerais
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease - CKD in stages 4 and 5 (Classification of the Brazilian Society of Nephrology), aged 18 years or older; both sexes; who have been undergoing Hemodialysis - HD for more than three months and three times a week
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Resistant and uncooperative patients, who do not have the cognitive conditions to respond to questionnaires and carry out assessments based on the criteria and cut-off points proposed by the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) and according to education; who present an unstable clinical condition; neurological diseases; and patients who complete 60% or less of the exercise protocol
Trial.Condition: low back pain; arterial stiffness; depression; fatigue
Trial.Intervention: This is a double-blind clinical trial with a convenience sample. The sampling method was convenience, including patients who met the study eligibility criteria. Data were collected by previously trained study researchers, initially at the hemodialysis unit at Minas Gerais University Hospital of Medical Sciences. The following sociodemographic and clinical data were compiled from the medical records: name, age, sex, marital status, number of comorbidities and medications used, chronic kidney disease stage, and time since hemodialysis initiation. These data will be used to identify and characterize the patients. At the first moment, the study was explained to the patient and when they indicated their desire to participate, the free and informed consent form was signed. Interviews were conducted with the patients during the hemodialysis session, using a questionnaire to collect demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical data, laboratory tests, and instruments for physical and functional assessment. The patients were divided into two groups: experimental (16 individuals) and control (16 individuals). All subjects underwent chest and lower limb circumference tests, modified sphygmomanometer test, Mobil-O-Graph, handgrip dynamometry, WHODAS 2.0 questionnaire, manovacuometry, ventilometry, Roland Morris questionnaire, Fatigue Severity Scale, visual analogue pain scale and Beck Depression Inventory in the first week, with three days of interview/data collection. From the following week onwards, for six weeks, three times a week, physiotherapeutic interventions were performed with aerobic, muscular strength and lung expansion exercises that enhance venous return during hemodialysis. At the end of six weeks, both groups underwent a reassessment with the same instruments applied on;G11.427.410.698.277 I03.350
Trial.Primary_outcome: To assess the level of functionality and disability, and the factors that negatively influence the execution of activities of daily living in patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing hemodialysis.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: To intervene with a physical exercise protocol based on muscle strength training, aerobic training and lung expansion during hemodialysis to optimize venous return and reduce the symptoms of this process. To apply an informative booklet on the exercises to be performed in an out-of-hospital environment. To evaluate the effect of the developed physical therapy protocol on the variables intensity of global and low back pain, respiratory parameters, depressive symptoms, arterial stiffness, fatigue, global strength, muscle strength and functionality. To evaluate whether the interventions were effective in reducing the symptoms of hemodialysis.
Trial.Source_Support: Faculdade Ciências Médicas de Minas Gerais
Trial.Secondary_Sponsor: Faculdade Ciências Médicas de Minas Gerais

Trial.Public_title: Benefits of tai chi training vs strength training combined with the mental stimulation of an ICOPE program on physical and mental functional capacity in older adults
Trial.Scientific_title: Effect of tai chi training vs strength training combines with mental stimulation on physical and cognitive functional capacity in older adults within the framework of ICOPE
Trial.Contact_Address: Batalla 5 de Mayo s/n esquina Fuerte de Loreto, Colonia Ejército de Oriente, Iztapalapa
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria:
Inclusion criteria: 1. Adults aged 60 to 74 years.
2. No uncontrolled chronic non-communicable diseases.
3. No severe cognitive problems assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCa) scale.
4. No terminal illnesses.
5. Sedentary in the past 6 months (less than 60 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week and no regular resistance training).
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria:
Exclusion criteria: 1. Older adults who do not wish to participate in the study.
2. Who do not have signed informed consent.
3. With uncontrolled chronic non-communicable diseases.
4. With limitations in physical or cognitive functional capacity.
Trial.Condition:
Physical and mental functional capacity in older adults
Other
Trial.Intervention:
All participants provide written informed consent before being included in the study. Groups will be randomly assigned using the Oxford Minimization and Randomization (OxMaR) software.

Group 1: Tai Chi combined with mental stimulation: taught over 8 weeks, Tai Chi 8-form and later 24-form training. It will be taught 4 days a week in 60-minute sessions in person. In addition, the class will be filmed so that people who cannot attend the in-person session can do the exercise at home.

Group 2: Strength training combined with mental stimulation: Multimodal exercise, including progressive strength training and other exercise components (balance, flexibility, and aerobic training), as recommended in the ICOPE guidelines. These sessions will be taught four days a week in 60-minute in-person sessions. In addition, the class will be filmed so that people who cannot attend the in-person session can do the exercise at home.
Physical training sessions design:
1. Warming: 5 minutes of joint lubrication and 5 minutes of activation exercise to increase heart rate (5 minutes).
2. Main exercise: This exercise will work on coordination, strength, and endurance, targeting the arms, legs, back, and other parts of the body (40 minutes).
3. Cool-down: Stretching and breathing exercises to improve flexibility and bring the body into a relaxed state (10 minutes).

Group 3: Older adults who are unable to participate in the physical exercise and mental stimulation program but who agree to participate in baseline, 6-month, and 12-month measurements of the study variables.

Mental stimulation program:
The program developed at the Gerontology Research Unit of the FES Zaragoza, UNAM, will be implemented. The program consists of 24 one-hour sessions once a week and includes activities to pre
Trial.Primary_outcome:
1. Cognitive functions measured using the Neuropsychological Assessment Battery: (i) Verbal fluency by category (animals); (ii) Memory using a 10-word list; (iii) Praxias; (iv) Trail Making tests A and B; (v) Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).
2. Physical performance assessed using the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB).
3. Body composition assessed using single-frequency bioelectrical impedance (BIA) using RJL equipment.
4. Muscle strength assessed using a Jamar handheld hydraulic dynamometer with a measurement range of 0 to 100 kg.
5. Biochemical markers of oxidative stress and inflammation: total pro-oxidant capacity, total antioxidant capacity, and markers of chronic inflammation (IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-a).
All measured at 12 months
Trial.Secondary_outcome:
1. Psychological variables and sleep: depressive symptoms, sleep, well-being, and quality of life will be assessed according to standardized protocols at the Gerontology Research Unit.
2. Advanced activities of daily living: The questionnaire to assess advanced activities of daily living developed by Dias et al. (2019) will be administered.
All measured at 12 months
Trial.results_ipd_description: Published as a supplement to the results publication. Datasets generated or analyzed during this study will be included in the subsequent publication of the results.

Trial.Scientific_title: Effects of scapular stabilization excercises on shoulder stability, common extensor tendon thickness, functional level, grip strength and pain in patients with lateral elbow tendinopathy
Trial.Study_design: Primary Purpose : Treatment, Intervention Model : Parallel, Blinding/Masking : Single, Blinding Target : Subject, Allocation : RCT
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Sahmyook University
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria:
Inclusion criteria: This study included 24 participants aged between 20 and 40 years who were diagnosed with lateral elbow tendinopathy and voluntarily agreed to participate in the study.
The inclusion criteria were adults aged 20 to 40 years with lateral elbow pain and a score of 3 or higher in the pain subscale of the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE). Additionally, participants had to meet at least three of the following six conditions:
(1) localized tenderness on palpation of the lateral epicondyle,
(2) pain elicited during Mill’s test,
(3) pain elicited during Maudsley’s test,
(4) pain elicited during Cozen’s test,
(5) pain during grip strength assessment with the elbow extended,
(6) a difference of more than 8% in grip strength between the flexed and extended elbow positions.
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Exclusion criteria included individuals who had undergone surgery on the wrist, elbow, or shoulder; those with symptoms of radiculopathy; those diagnosed with systemic arthritis or rheumatoid arthritis; individuals with neurological deficits; those who had received injection therapy in the affected area within the past three months; those with metal implants in the wrist, shoulder, or elbow; those with severe skin lesions on the back or elbow; and those who did not consent to participate in this study.
Trial.Condition: ;Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue
Trial.Intervention:
Behavioral : The wrist extensor exercise program consisted of three exercises, each performed for 3 sets of 15 repetitions, taking approximately 20 minutes to complete. The scapular stabilization exercise program included five exercises, each also performed for 3 sets of 15 repetitions, requiring about 25 minutes.

In the experimental group, both the wrist extensor exercise program and the scapular stabilization exercise program were implemented twice a week for six weeks, totaling 12 sessions. In contrast, the control group performed only the wrist extensor exercise program twice a week for six weeks.
Trial.Primary_outcome: Korean version of the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE) questionnaire;Korean version of the Quick Disabilities of the Arm;grip strength;pain visual analog scale
Trial.Secondary_outcome: Closed Kinetic Chain Upper Extremity Stability Test (CKCUEST); Thickness of the lower trapezius muscle;Thickness of the common extensor tendon

Trial.Public_title: A Study on the Muscle Activity around the Shoulder according to the Change in Pressure Strength during Blood Flow Restriction Shoulder Stabilization Exercise
Trial.Scientific_title: The effect of acute blood flow restriction-shoulder stability exercises around the shoulder muscle activation by changing in compressive intensity
Trial.Study_design: Primary Purpose : Prevention, Intervention Model : Parallel, Blinding/Masking : Open, Allocation : RCT
Trial.Contact_Address: 815, Hwarang-ro, Nowon-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Sahmyook University
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria:
Inclusion criteria: 1.No orthopedic conditions
2.No limitations in joint range of motion
3.No current medical conditions affecting measurements
4. no current trauma or pain
5. understand the purpose of this study and agree to participate in the study
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria:
Exclusion criteria: 1.Subjects with musculoskeletal conditions such as shoulders and elbows
2.Subjects who are unable to exercise on their own
3.Subjects with past or present cardiovascular disease
4.Subjects who are unable to perform the stabilization exercise positions of this study
5.Subjects who do not agree to participate in this study
Trial.Intervention:
Behavioral : Twenty-four subjects who met the inclusion criteria were selected to participate in the study. Before the experiment, the participants' general characteristics such as gender, age, weight, height, dominant arm, and body mass index were collected, and their systolic blood pressure was measured, which would later affect the pressure intensity of the blood flow restriction exercise. Subjects' pre- and post-assessment measures of muscular endurance, strength, range of motion, and muscle activity in shoulder external rotation were then measured. Electrodes were placed on the supraspinatus, teres minor, infraspinatus, and infraspinatus to normalize muscle activity, and maximum velocity isometric contractions were measured based on the work of Alpert et al (2000). Two of the 26 subjects complained of pain in the shoulder joint during the measurements and were excluded because they did not meet the inclusion criteria of no current trauma or pain.
Subjects were randomly assigned to the blood flow restricted low-intensity shoulder external rotation exercise group and the low-intensity shoulder external rotation exercise group by lottery for men and women. The exercise program of the experimental group and the control group consisted of a warm-up and the main exercise, and was based on the guidelines for shoulder stabilization exercises (american academy of orthopaedic surgeons 2022). Trial.Public_title: Efficacy of laser treatment for obstructive sleep apnea - clinical trial
Trial.Scientific_title: Efficacy of non-ablative treatment with combination of Nd:YAG and Er:YAG lasers for sleep-disordered breathing analyzed by clinical and molecular parameters - controlled, randomized, double-blind clinical trial
Trial.Primary_sponsor: Faculdade de Odontologia da Universidade de São Paulo
Trial.Study_design: a phase n/a, randomized-controlled, double-blind, parallel, treatment
Trial.Contact_Address: Avenida Professor Lineu Prestes, 2242 - Centro de Lasers e Aplicações
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Instituto de Pesquisas Energéticas e Nucleares - IPEN
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Men and women; aged between 25 and 65 years; regardless of race or social class; who are at risk of obstructive sleep apnea by screening with the Stopbang questionnaire; with a minimum wash out of six months for other therapies for sleep-disordered breathing; who agree to participate in the study with signature of the free and informed consent form
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Undergoing medical treatment or treatment for sleep-related breathing disorders; smokers; alcoholics; cancer patients; with diagnosed lung problems; with heart disease; using more than two antihypertensive drugs; with pharyngeal or nasal obstructions that require strictly surgical resolution; with previous surgery in the oropharynx region; pregnant or lactating women; history of photosensitivity (allergies); using photosensitive medication; Body mass index (BMI) above 40 kg/m2; participants who are unable to attend treatment sessions or follow-up appointments; or who do not perform follow-up exams as indicated by the researchers
Trial.Intervention: This is a randomized, controlled, double-blind, parallel-arm clinical trial. Participants (men and women between 25 and 65 years of age, regardless of race or social class, with sleep-disordered breathing) will be selected after approval by the Research Ethics Committee, using the Stop-Bang questionnaire. All participants must sign the Informed Consent Form. Patients will be allocated to the laser or control groups using a sequence of random numbers generated by an external researcher, in a blocked format (10 blocks with 13 participants). Allocation confidentiality will be guaranteed by the strategy of inserting participant data into Craft paper envelopes and then sealing them (by the external researcher). Each envelope will be randomly assigned a number (by the external researcher). Those who enroll participants in the study, as well as the researcher who will perform the interventions, will not have access to this information. Evaluators of the main outcome and participants will be blind to the allocation of groups and proposed interventions. The sample size was determined according to a pilot study with a similar population with sleep-disordered breathing. The calculation was performed considering the reduction in the oxyhemoglobin desaturation index (ODI) as the primary outcome. Since the data did not follow a normal distribution in that study, the interquartile range (88%) was considered instead of the standard deviation. A sample power of 80% with a two-tailed type 1 error of 0.05 was determined. Since, according to the literature, a reduction equal to or greater than 50% of the initial ODI value is considered successful in the treatment of SDB, a value of 50% was stipulated for the minimum difference to be detected in the sample calculation. Using the tool on the;E02.594
Trial.Primary_outcome: As the main outcome, we will evaluate the variation in the oxyhemoglobin desaturation index. The oxyhemoglobin desaturation index reflects the number of obstructive events per hour of sleep. The lower the value of the index, the better the patient's health status
Trial.Secondary_outcome: The variation in sleep time with snoring that is positively related to the severity of the respiratory disorder (the noise is a consequence of the respiratory effort to overcome the imposed tissue resistance);The variation in the peak amplitude of the snoring noise that is positively related to the severity of the respiratory disorder (the noise is a consequence of the respiratory effort to overcome the imposed tissue resistance);Variation in spectral analysis of potential biomarkers for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Spectral analysis of potential biomarkers for obstructive sleep apnea is not yet well established in the literature, but there is evidence that alpha-amylase may be more pronounced after a night with many respiratory obstruction events;Score variation of the Stopbang questionnaire for screening for risk of obstructive sleep apnea;Variation in Epworth Daytime Sleepiness Perception Questionnaire Score;The variation in upper airway lumen according to the modified Mallampati Classification. The upper airway lumen is a predictor of severity for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The smaller the lumen for the passage of breathing air, the greater the risk for obstructive sleep apnea
Trial.Source_Support: Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Cientifico e Tecnológico
Trial.Secondary_Sponsor: Sistema Nacional de Laboratórios de Fotônica;Beauty Smile, Clinica Dental Laser

Sensitive data, that is, data protected by privacy laws, will be kept confidential, such as the identity of the participants, photographic records, snoring sounds, and other exams that may identify the participant. To protect the study data, there will be access control and regular backups. To request and grant access to the research data, a cover letter with the intention, name of the researcher in charge, affiliation and request form must be sent. If approved by the research committee, access will be granted. Access to the data, records of download activities and use will be monitored. The research data management plan will be disclosed to the public through the publication of the research protocol, where it will be included. Users will be notified about the policies and procedures for accessing the data

Trial.Public_title: Can Slow and Smooth Squats Improve Strength and Movement in Older Adults?
Trial.Scientific_title: Effects of Dynamic Steadiness Squat Training on Force Steadiness and Physical Function in Older Adults - SMILE (Steady Movement Improving Lower-body Efficacy) Study
Trial.Primary_sponsor: Osaka University of Health and Sport Sciences
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Osaka University of Health and Sport Sciences School of Sport Sciences
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria:
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Participants will be excluded from the study if they meet any of the following conditions: 1. Engaged in resistance training or high-intensity exercise within the past year. 2. Unable to commit to a training schedule of three sessions per week for eight weeks. 3. Diagnosed by a physician with a neurological or cardiovascular disease. 4. Advised by a physician to restrict physical activity for any reason. 5. Deemed by the investigators to be unsuitable for participation in the study. Control3 1. Individuals who have been medically advised to avoid exercise, or who have injuries/disabilities that hinder exercise. 2. Individuals who habitually engage in strength training.
Trial.Intervention:
In the Dynamic Steadiness Squat Training group, a small wireless accelerometer connected to a tablet will be attached to the lateral surface of the participant's thigh. The angular velocity of the thigh will be displayed on the tablet in real time. Participants will perform bodyweight squats while viewing the real-time angular velocity displacement of their thigh on the tablet screen. During the squats, participants will be instructed to complete the downward and upward phases in 5 seconds each, and to consciously keep the variability of their thigh's angular velocity within a specified range. At home, participants will perform the same squat training as smoothly as possible, with an emphasis on minimizing unnecessary fluctuations.
In the Conventional Squat Training group, participants will be instructed to perform slow-paced squats at home. Each training session will consist of 3 to 5 sets of 10 repetitions.
To compare intervention training for Intervention 1 and Intervention 2, habitually untrained males and females in their 20s and 30s will serve as a control group and will not undergo any training.
Trial.Primary_outcome: 1. Assessment of Force Steadiness During Squatting Force steadiness during squatting will be assessed by measuring thigh angular velocity using an inertial sensor on the thigh. Variability in angular velocity will quantify force steadiness. Lower-limb muscle activity will also be assessed using surface electromyography (EMG).
Trial.Secondary_outcome: 2. Isometric Knee Extension and Flexion Strength Testing Isometric knee extension and flexion strength will be measured with an isokinetic dynamometer. Muscle activity during testing will also be recorded via surface EMG. 3. Assessment of Lower-Limb Proprioception Knee joint proprioception will be assessed by quantifying the difference between perceived and actual knee joint angles using an isokinetic dynamometer. This will evaluate changes in joint position sense. 4. Chair Rise Test Participants will perform 10 repetitions of a sit-to-stand movement from a chair with a backrest, standing completely and sitting back down. The total time will be measured. 5. Stair Climb Test Participants will ascend and descend a four-step flight of stairs as quickly and safely as possible, without handrails. The time from start to end will be recorded. 6. Single-Leg Stance with Eyes Open Participants will stand barefoot on a force plate with hands on hips. While lifting the non-tested leg approximately 5 cm, the duration of balance maintained on the tested leg will be measured. 7. Timed Up and Go (TUG) Test Participants will sit in a chair with armrests, then stand, walk 3 meters at a comfortable fast pace, turn, return, and sit down. The total time from standing up to re-seating will be recorded. 8. Force Steadiness During Isometric Contraction Force steadiness will be measured during 12-second isometric contractions at 10% and 2.5% of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC). Lower limb muscle activity will also be assessed using surface EMG. 9. Force Steadiness During Concentric and Eccentric Contraction Seated participants will have an inertial sensor on the lower leg to measure angular velocity during knee extension and flexion. Variability in angular velocity will quantify force steadiness. Lower limb muscle activity will also be evaluated using surface EMG.
Trial.Source_Support: Osaka University of Health and Sport Sciences

Trial.Intervention:
Current interventions as of 19/12/2025:

The researchers are recruiting 126 patients as part of an observational study to look at the association between functional dyspepsia and ultra-processed food. Among these 126, 24 will be recruited to take part in the interventional proportion, which will be testing a minimally processed food diet and its impact on gastrointestinal symptoms.

Patients initially screened for the observational study (V1) complete a medical assessment and a series of questionnaires, then exit the study. Among those with the highest intake of ultraprocessed food based on the Intake24 dietary recall questionnaire (=50%), they will be invited to take part in the intervention. This will be a minimally processed food diet, provided by researchers/dietitians/psychologists, which involves education, behavioural changes, recipe advice, leaflets and motivational interviewing at baseline and then 1- and 3-months follow-up. These will be face-to-face. The sessions will be centred around ultra-processed food and will be tailored to the needs of the individual (e.g. work schedule, dietary requirements, cooking skills, finances).

Inflammatory Bowel Disease ;Oral and Gastrointestinal - Inflammatory bowel disease;Oral and Gastrointestinal - Crohn's disease
Trial.Intervention:
Dietitian-led, Open-label program of 3 dietary strategies as adjunctive therapy for Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

Dietary therapy will be offered to patients: the Crohn’s Disease Exclusion Diet (if the patient has Crohn’s or pouchitis), the Ulcerative Colitis diet (if the patient has UC or microscopic colitis), or a less restrictive wholefood diet that excludes ultra-processed food (for any condition).

The Crohn’s Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED)
The Crohn’s Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED) is a 3-phase diet. The diet mainly focuses on:
• Avoidance of added chemicals
• Inclusion of high-quality, low-fat protein (mostly chicken and eggs)
• Inclusion of resistant starch and specific fibres (apples, bananas, potatoes)
• Use of liquid supplements to help meet energy and nutrient needs

Behavioral, Others(Exercise or Phyiscal activity intervetnion ) : This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of an evidence-based exercise program incorporating the Picture Exchange Communication System (PECS) to enhance physical activity and reduce problematic behaviors in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

A total of 20 children with ASD aged 8 to 13 will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n = 10) or the control group (n = 10), stratified by age and severity of disability.

The intervention group will participate in a structured PECS-based exercise program for 8 weeks, 3 sessions per week, totaling 24 sessions including pre- and post-assessments. Each session will last 60 minutes. Participants will select exercises using PECS, and the activities will focus on gross motor skill enhancement under instructor guidance.

The control group will maintain their usual daily activities and routines without additional interventions and will undergo the same pre- and post-assessments.

Outcome measures include anthropometric indices, body composition, physical activity levels, blood markers, motor function, and frequency of problematic behaviors.

Trial.Scientific_title: Effects of lumbar spine manipulation on pain, proprioception, muscle strength and balance in patients with patellofemoral pain syndrome
Trial.Study_design: Primary Purpose : Treatment, Intervention Model : Parallel, Blinding/Masking : Double, Blinding Target : Subject, Investigator, Allocation : RCT
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Sahmyook University
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: The selection criteria for research participants included individuals who experienced knee pain in two or more activities such as climbing stairs, squatting, prolonged sitting, running, and squatting, as well as individuals scoring three or more points in the Clarke test for knee pain.
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Individuals with a history of patellar dislocation or fracture, those who underwent lower limb surgery four months ago, individuals with spinal disorders, lumbar nerve or muscle disorders, or symptoms of nerve compression are excluded.
Trial.Condition: ;Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue
Trial.Intervention:
Procedure/Surgery : The subject was instructed to have the painful knee raised upward and hold onto the wrist. They were positioned close to the edge of the treatment table with the therapist. The therapist extended the subject's lower leg, while the upper leg was flexed at a 90° angle, with the foot placed behind the lower knee.

The therapist stood at a 45° angle facing the subject and made contact with the upper knee using one of the subject's lower knees. Subsequently, the therapist straddled the subject's flexed knee and made contact with the mid-shin of the subject using their thigh.

The therapist's cephalic (toward the head) hand made contact with the subject's lateral aspect of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra beneath the subject's thigh. The caudal (toward the tail) hand held the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra like a hook, making contact with the subject's posterior lateral buttock and the femur using their forearm. The two-handed technique secured from the inside to the outside and from below to above. The caudal hand in contact with the posterior lateral buttock and femur was drawn from the outside to the inside. When it reached the point of maximum tension, the therapist utilized their entire body, both upper and lower limbs, to perform one correction.

If no audible correction sound was heard, an additional attempt was made, and afterward, it was considered corrected.
Trial.Primary_outcome: pressure pain thresholds;muscle power
Trial.Secondary_outcome: proprioception;dynamic balance

Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Participants in this study were healthy adult males aged between 20 and 29 years who had not been exposed to high-altitude environments within the past six months and had no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, or immune-related diseases. Only individuals who received a full explanation of the study’s purpose and procedures, understood the information provided, and voluntarily agreed to participate were included.
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Individuals were excluded if they had been diagnosed with or were receiving treatment for cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, or immune-related diseases; had musculoskeletal disorders that could limit exercise performance; had a history of altitude sickness or exhibited sensitivity to high-altitude environments; reported discomfort or intolerance when exercising in hot, cold, or hypobaric hypoxic environments; or were judged by the investigators to have any condition that could compromise the safety of the intervention or the accuracy of the measurements.
Trial.Intervention: Others(Exercise in various environmental conditions (Heat, Cold, Hypobaric hypoxia)) : This experimental study was conducted using a randomized crossover design to compare acute exercise responses under three different environmental conditions—heat, cold, and hypobaric hypoxia—in healthy adult males. Each participant completed one exercise session in each condition, with a minimum 7-day washout period between sessions to minimize order effects. The exercise intervention was applied identically across all conditions. After a 30-minute resting adaptation period in each environment, participants performed a graded exercise test (GXT) to exhaustion using a cycle ergometer (Aerobike 75XL III, Combi Wellness, Japan) at a fixed cadence of 60 rpm, starting at 50 W with incremental increases of 25 W every 2 minutes. In Study 1 (heat condition), exercise was conducted at 20°C, 30°C, and 40°C; in Study 2 (cold condition), at 20°C, 10°C, and 0°C; with humidity maintained at 50 ± 5% for both. In Study 3 (hypobaric hypoxia condition), exercise was performed in a hypobaric chamber (NCTC-1, Nara Control, Seoul, Korea) under simulated altitudes of 0 m, 1,500 m, 3,000 m, and 4,500 m, corresponding to atmospheric pressures of approximately 760, 630, 526, and 429 mmHg, respectively. The chamber conditions were maintained at 20 ± 1°C temperature and 50 ± 5% humidity. During all sessions, physiological responses—such as respiratory gas exchange, cardiac function, and skeletal muscle oxygenation—were assessed at rest, ventilatory threshold (VT), respiratory compensation point (RCP), and at maximal exercise. Additionally, immune-related blood markers (e.g., inflammatory cytokines, HSP70) were measured before and after exercise. The main differences among interventions were the variations in en

Trial.Public_title: A proposal for an ecological assessment of the affective response to increasing and decreasing intensity physical exercise in adolescents
Trial.Scientific_title: The affective response to physical exercise of different intensities in adolescents
Trial.Primary_sponsor: União Brasileira de Educação e Assistência
Trial.Study_design: a phase n/a, randomized-controlled, n/a, cross-over, prevention
Trial.Contact_Address: Av. Ipiranga, 6681 - Partenon, Porto Alegre - RS
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Healthy volunteers; both genders; aged between 11 and 17 years; agree to participate in the study by signing the consent forms by their guardian and assent by the participant
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Self-report of diagnosis of psychiatric disorders; self-report of use of alcohol or drugs; physical inability to perform physical exercise; participant who does not participate in any stage of the study
Trial.Intervention: This is a randomized crossover clinical study with a minimum of 17 adolescents (aged between 11 and 17 years) in which the same participants will perform the two exercise protocols in an ecological environment (multi-sports court), increasing and decreasing intensity. Data collection will take place in 3 different meetings, separated by 1 week between them (washout period between protocols to minimize the carry-over effect (residues) of sequence), these being (1) physical assessment (Psychophysiology Assessment, Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire, Affective Exercise Experiences (AFFEXX) Questionnaire, Preference for and Tolerance of the Intensity of Exercise Questionnaire, International Physical Activity Questionnaire and Anthropometrics measures) and maximum physical effort capacity test (Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 – YYIR1); (2) experimental protocol of 15 minutes of aerobic physical exercise (PE) in an ecological environment (multi-sports court), similar to the Yo Yo test protocol, with increasing intensity (with intensity increasing every five minutes, light, moderate and vigorous) and; (3) decreasing (order of exercise intensities inversely proportional to the increasing condition, with vigorous intensity at the beginning, in the fifth minute reducing to moderate and in the 10th minute decreasing to light intensity). After the 1st meeting (physical evaluation) the participants will be randomly grouped in the sequence one (protocol of increasing intensity followed by decreasing intensity) or two (protocol of decreasing intensity followed by increasing intensity) through the website www.randomizer.org, thus avoiding order bias. The participants will not know in advance to which group they were assigned. The intensity of the experimental protocols ;F01.470.867; G11.427.410.698.277;F04.711.336
Trial.Primary_outcome: It is expected that adolescents who practice the exercise session at decreasing intensity will present a more positive affective response during and, especially at the end of the session, which will tend to provide a remembered pleasure with a more positive valence, as well as a perception of a promising anticipated pleasure, replicating previous studies in a laboratory environment, providing the applicability of a protocol for evaluating affect at different intensities in an environment closer to the real one. Furthermore, this affective memory of the exercise may reverse valence after 30 minutes, due to the return to the basal state.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: More positive affective responses are expected in adolescents considered physically active and with a higher level of physical fitness. Furthermore, it is believed that the waist-to-height ratio and muscle mass index (BMI) may be variables that will interfere in the intensity-affect relationship, providing more positive responses in eutrophic individuals. It is also worth noting that previous preferences for exercise may moderate and/or mediate this relationship between exercise and affect in the population studied. Finally, socioeconomic factors may also interfere in the psychological perception of physical exercise.
Trial.Source_Support: Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES)
Trial.Secondary_Sponsor: Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul

Trial.Public_title: The role of progressive overload in the development of strength and muscle mass
Trial.Scientific_title: Effect of overload progression of strength training on strength and muscle mass
Trial.Primary_sponsor: Centro de Ciências Biológicas e da Saúde da Universidade Federal de São Carlos
Trial.Study_design: a phase n/a, randomized-controlled, single-blind, other, treatment
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Universidade Federal de São Carlos
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Healthy young adults aged 18 to 30; of both sexes; no previous experience in Resistance Training
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Participants must not have engaged in resistance training during the six months prior to the study; they must not have any musculoskeletal injuries in the lower limbs or neuromuscular disorders that could interfere with the execution of the study protocols
Trial.Intervention: This is a within-subject randomized controlled trial (two arms), single-blind. The two interventions being compared (PROG and NPROG) will be performed on the same individual concomitantly (each leg will undergo one intervention). Thus, 30 participants (i.e., 60 legs) will be allocated to both interventions. However, the sequence of allocation of each participant’s leg between interventions will be determined using stratified randomization based only on leg dominance. One leg of each participant will be randomly assigned to an intervention, while the contralateral leg will automatically be assigned to the other. The order of intervention application within a training session will be randomized and counterbalanced throughout the study. Both limbs (i.e., experimental units) will undergo a 12-week lower-limb resistance training program consisting of 24 training sessions of unilateral knee extension exercise using an extensor chair (Effort NKR; Nakagym, São Paulo, Brazil), performed twice a week, with a minimum of 48 hours between sessions. All training sessions will begin with a 5-minute general warm-up on a cycle ergometer (Ergo-Fit; Pirmasens, Rheinland-Pfalz, Germany) at 20 km·h?¹. The initial load will be established through one familiarization session. Both groups (PROG and NPROG) will train within a predefined repetition range of 10–12 RM. In the PROG condition, load adjustments will be made to ensure that maximal effort is maintained within this repetition range. However, in the NPROG condition, the overload will remain constant, regardless of any changes in the participant’s effort perception.;E02.760.169.063.500.387.875
Trial.Primary_outcome: Vastus lateralis muscle cross-sectional area measured by B-mode ultrasonography.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: Volume load and rated perceived exertion measured by OMNI and repetitions in reserve (RIR) scales.

Trial.Intervention: This is an experimental study with a crossover design, non-blind, consisting of two acute interventions (two arms) of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, with and without a dual cognitive task.The research will be carried out in three stages: 1) initial assessments (characterization of participants), 2) and 3) pre-intervention assessments, aerobic training session (AT) and/or dual-task aerobic training (TAD) and post-intervention assessments. intervention. The elderly participated in two training sessions in a planned order, which will be held seven days apart. The interventions will be carried out on a horizontal exercise bike and will last 50 minutes each. Exercise intensity will be moderate with 60 to 70 per cent of maximum heart rate. In TA, the session will focus only on aerobic training and in TAD, cognitive tasks will be added. BDNF will be collected through blood and laboratory tests using the multiplex microsphere immunofluorimetric test (ProcartaPlex Multiplex Immunoassay, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) for the Luminex platform (MAGPIX, Luminex Corp., Austin, TX, USA ), carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and reference values. This study is expected to provide information on the acute effects of dual cognitive tasks associated with aerobic exercise on the functioning of the cognitive system and neurotrophic factors in physically independent elderly people, with and without mild cognitive impairment. Trial.Public_title: Evaluation of the longevity of cone morse dental implants
Trial.Scientific_title: Evaluation of the longevity of dental implants installed at the Integrated Clinic of the Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Patients over the age of 18; both genders; with single or total Arcsys® implants; with a history of progress and imaging tests such as tomography and panoramic scans
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Patients who cannot undergo imaging tests, such as pregnant women
Trial.Intervention: This is an observational, longitudinal and retrospective study. It will evaluate a group of 84 patients seen at the Integrated Clinic of the Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense between 2018 and 2020. The patients, whose implants were installed around 5 to 7 years ago, will undergo a clinical consultation to check their oral health. A radiographic examination will be carried out in order to confirm bone integrity around the implant(s) and a form will be applied to extract information related to quality of life. The success rate of the implants will be determined based on the absence of pain, the absence of implant mobility and bone loss within acceptable thresholds - loss of less than 1.5mm in the first year and less than 0.2mm per year after the first 12 months. Age, systematic conditions and the presence of infectious or inflammatory processes will also be taken into account in the analysis. The first results, obtained in June 2025, show that 65 implants were evaluated in 26 patients. The sample was predominantly composed of women (61.5%), with a higher concentration in the age group of 62 to 69 years (42.3%). The survival rate of the implants was 100%, with no reports of loss. Post-operative complications were rare (7.6%), including one case of psychological trauma and one case of transient peri-implant inflammation. The majority of patients (96.2%) did not report pain or discomfort in the implant area, and 84.6% did not face difficulties in chewing. All participants reported improvement in quality of life, with an average satisfaction level of 9.5 on a scale of 1 to 10. Tomographic analysis demonstrated excellent bone integration in all cases, with maintenance of peri-implant bone volume and absence of radiolucency at the bone-implant interface;E06.780.346.593;V03.175.500
Trial.Primary_outcome: Based on the analysis of radiographic examinations, the measurement of bone loss and mobility, it is expected that the success rate of implant installation will be greater than 95%.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: No secondary outcomes expected
Trial.Source_Support: FGM Dental Group;Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense

Trial.Public_title: VALENF-HAD: optimizing nursing assessment in hospital-at-home units
Trial.Scientific_title: Development and validation of a comprehensive meta-instrument for assessing functional capacity, risk of pressure injuries, risk of falls, frailty, nutritional status, suspected dysphagia, and sleep quality in patients admitted to hospital-at-home units, based on the analysis of other validated nursing assessment tools
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria:
Inclusion criteria: 1. The patient undergoing assessment must be over 18 years of age
2. Nursing assessments must be conducted within the first 24–48 hours after admission to the hospital-at-home unit
3. Patients who voluntarily agree to participate in the study and sign the Informed Consent Form, or in cases of disability, their primary caregiver
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria:
Exclusion criteria: 1. Nursing assessments of patients who are not expected to remain in the hospital-at-home unit for more than 48 hours.
2. Patients who are frequently readmitted for the administration of recurrent treatments, such as:
2.1. Transfusion support
2.2. Medication delivery under a day-hospital model
Trial.Condition:
To develop and validate a comprehensive meta-instrument for the assessment of functional capacity, risk of pressure injuries, risk of falls, frailty, nutritional status, suspected dysphagia, and sleep in patients admitted to hospital-at-home units.
Injury, Occupational Diseases, Poisoning
Trial.Intervention:
This is a multicenter, cross-sectional study aimed at developing and validating a meta-instrument that consolidates various nursing assessment tools used in hospital-at-home units to evaluate functional capacity, risk of pressure injuries, risk of falls, frailty, nutritional status, and sleep quality. The study will be conducted across the four public hospitals in the province of Castellón, with an estimated duration of three years.

The study population will consist of patients admitted to hospital-at-home units. Nursing assessments will be included if they meet the following inclusion criteria: patients over 18 years of age undergoing evaluation; assessment performed within the first 24–48 hours of admission; and informed consent provided for participation in the study. Assessments will be excluded if patients are not expected to remain in the unit for more than 48 hours, such as those frequently readmitted for recurrent treatments like transfusion support or medication administration under a day-hospital model. A sample size of 1,180 participants has been calculated.

The study will include sociodemographic variables and variables related to the care process. The assessment variables linked to hospitalization-related issues include: functional capacity (Barthel Index and Lawton & Brody Scale); risk of pressure injuries (Braden Scale); risk of falls (STRATIFY Scale); VALENF Instrument; frailty (FRAIL Questionnaire); nutritional status (Nutritional Screening Initiative tool); suspected dysphagia (Eating Assessment Tool); and sleep quality (Athens Insomnia Scale).

Data collection will be carried out using the Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) software following patient admission, based on routine nursing assessments and through consecutive sampling.

First, a d
Trial.Primary_outcome:
The nursing assessment meta-instrument will be developed by consolidating data collected by the following assessment tools within the first 24–48 hours after admission:
1. Barthel Index
2. Lawton and Brody Scale
3. Braden Scale
4. STRATIFY Scale
5. FRAIL Questionnaire
6. Nutritional Screening Initiative Tool
7. Eating Assessment Tool
8. Athens Insomnia Scale
Trial.Secondary_outcome: The psychometric properties of the new meta-instrument will be examined, including content validity, construct validity, internal consistency, and inter-rater reliability using data collected during the study at one timepoint

Trial.Public_title: Blood flow restriction exercise therapy for people with obesity
Trial.Scientific_title: Effects of blood flow restriction training on metabolomics and proteomics in patients with obesity
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria:
Inclusion criteria: 1. Aged 18-25 years
2. Body fat percentage greater than 30%
3. No long-term medication, smoking, or excessive drinking habits
4. No exercise-related contraindications, such as cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, respiratory system diseases, etc
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Suffering from any illness that is not suitable for participating in sports
Trial.Condition:
Exercise and metabolic improvement in obese adolescents
Nutritional, Metabolic, Endocrine
Trial.Intervention: Participants were randomly assigned to two experimental groups (M and B) and one control group (C) by drawing lots. The intervention period lasted for a total of 12 weeks, with three sessions per week. Researchers monitored the heart rate (HR) and blood oxygen saturation during exercise to ensure the safety of participants. Initially, participants were required to perform a 10-minute warm-up activity at an intensity of 50 W on an aerobic power bike. Following the warm-up, participants in all exercise groups engaged in continuous exercise at 60% of their maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) intensity, maintaining a speed of 60±5 revolutions per minute (RPM), until they overcame a mechanical work of 200kj. A 10-minute cool-down activity was required after the exercise. B group was required to apply a 60% limb occlusive pressure (LOP) using an inflatable cuff (Ariband, Australia) at the proximal inguinal region of both legs based on the exercise protocol of the M group. During exercise, the participants' subjective perceived exertion (RPE) and heart rate (HR) were recorded every 5 minutes. The C group did not receive any exercise intervention throughout the entire intervention period.
Trial.Primary_outcome:
Measured at baseline and after the intervention:
1. Plasma non-targeted metabolomics data is measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)
2. Plasma proteomics data is measured using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)
3. Plasma-targeted metabolomics data is measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)
Trial.Secondary_outcome:
Measured 3 weeks before the start of the intervention and during the 12-week intervention period:
1. Daily dietary intake measured using a questionnaire every weekend
2. Physical activity measured using a questionnaire every weekend
3. Aerobic capacity is measured using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), typically with a cycle ergometer, to determine VO2 max (maximal oxygen uptake)
4. Body composition is measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)
5. Abdominal subcutaneous fat area is measured using computed tomography (CT) scans
6. Visceral fat area is measured using computed tomography (CT) scans
Trial.results_ipd_description: Published as a supplement to the results publication. The datasets generated and analysed during the current study will be published as a supplement to the results publication.

Overweight
Insulin resistance

Trial.Intervention:
The high-fat diet consisted of 30% carbohydrates, 20% protein, and 50% fat, with fat comprising 1:1:1 monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, and saturated fat.
For the high-fat diet plus branched-chain amino acids (BCAA), we added 0.1/kg/day of branched-chain amino acids to the participant’s high-fat diet. We used Dymatize’s BCAA Complex 2200 capsules in the BCAA group; each capsule contains leucine 275mg, isoleucine 137.5mg and valine 137.5mg. Capsule count was performed at the end of the 14-day intervention. The participants were randomized into the diet groups, and the metabolic kitchen provided three meals per day. The participants ate breakfast at the investigational unit and brought the remaining two meals home. The meals were prepared as ready-to-go. Participants were required to take a photograph of the food taken each day and to log any additional food. To increase compliance, the menu consisted of locally available and commonly consumed foods that most subjects could identify with. Students who screened positive for insomnia (ISI greater or equal to 15) were offered five weekly group sessions of psychologist-delivered cognitive behaviour therapy for insomnia (CBT-I). Structural changes: The team supported schools in adjusting their school schedules, recommending changes to sleep and wake times, reducing the duration of evening prep sessions and delaying the school morning start time later to better align with recommended national school schedule guidelines and sleep durations for adolescents. Trial.Public_title: Change in grip strength induced by overflow contralateral to hip flexion
Trial.Scientific_title: Change in grip strength induced by overflow contralateral to hip flexion
Trial.Study_design: a phase n/a, randomized-controlled, double-blind, parallel, other
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Universidade de São Paulo
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: They were aged between 18 and 30 and had a motor preference for the right upper limb.
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Volunteers with orthopaedic alterations, pain, difficulty in performing the palmar grasp and hip flexion movements, and failure to achieve at least 70 per cent of the maximum hip flexion force.
Trial.Intervention: This is a two-arm, double-blind, randomized controlled trial with a total of 90 participants, 45 in the control group and 45 in the treatment group. Control Group (CG): Individuals in this group will first establish a strength baseline by performing three contractions on a hand dynamometer. The right upper limb is used first, followed by the left upper limb, with a 60-second rest between limbs. The contractions of the same limb will be 6 seconds of effort and 10 seconds of rest. After establishing the baseline, the control group subjects will rest for 10 minutes and then repeat the same test to assess handgrip strength. Treatment Group: First, subjects in this group will establish a strength baseline by performing three contractions on a hand dynamometer, first on the right upper limb and then on the left upper limb, with a 60-second rest between the limbs. The contractions of the same limb will be 6 seconds of effort and 10 seconds of rest. For the treatment group, after the three contractions that made up the baseline (in each hand), the participants will perform three resisted isometric hip flexions (70% CIVM) for 6 seconds, with a 10-second rest between them, and simultaneously three palm grip contractions with the respective contralateral hand. The protocol will be performed first on the left lower limb, trying to radiate the force to the right upper limb, and then on the right lower limb to the left upper limb.The equipment where the subjects will perform the flexor isometry and the consequent production of overflow between the upper limbs was designed in our laboratory using fixed bands attached to a Dyna MopFitpulley dynamometer (so that the flexion force of the iliopsoas muscle could be quantified and later analyzed) anchored to the floor. The apparatus in whic;G11.427.410.698.277;G11.427.550
Trial.Primary_outcome: Expected outcome 1: We hope to identify whether muscle strength irradiation techniques, induced by resisted isometric contraction of the hip flexors at 70% of the maximum voluntary isometric contraction, could positively interfere with the handgrip strength measured contralaterally. ;Expected outcome 2: It was hoped to observe an attenuation of the progressive reduction in strength over multiple repeated maximal tests.;Outcome found 1: Strength maintenance was more evident in the test phase, suggesting that the contralateral irradiation resulting from isometric hip flexion mitigated neuromuscular fatigue in the upper limbs.;Outcome found 2: It was observed that the participants in the irradiation group showed a significant attenuation in the reduction of handgrip strength (p < 0.05) during the maximum repeated tests, compared to the control group.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: No secondary outcomes were expected
Trial.results_summary: he study aimed to assess the effects of motor overflow on handgrip strength. The overflow group showed a significant reduction in strength in the baseline phase but maintained higher strength during the test phase compared to the control group. The data suggest that motor overflow induced by contralateral hip flexion can help preserve handgrip strength during repetitive maximal efforts. The results indicate the potential application of motor overflow strategies in neuromuscular rehabilitation.
Trial.results_baseline_char: The baseline characteristics of the 107 participants (aged 18–30 years) included a balanced distribution of sex, with 52 males and 55 females. The participants were randomly assigned to the control group (C), which consisted of 53 individuals, and the overflow group (O), which consisted of 54 individuals. The groups showed similar anthropometric characteristics, including weight and height, with no significant differences between the groups (p > 0.05). Handgrip strength measurements were recorded during the baseline phase. For the control group, the average handgrip strength was 533.08 N for males and 316.11 N for females, while the overflow group had an average handgrip strength of 493.9 N for males and 322.24 N for females. All participants were right-handed, as assessed by the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory.
Trial.results_adverse_events: No serious adverse events were reported during the study. Minor adverse events included mild discomfort in the hands and hip region during the experimental protocol, but no participant experienced persistent clinical complications.
Trial.results_outcome_measures: The primary outcome measure was handgrip strength (HGS), assessed using a hand dynamometer during two phases (baseline and test). In the test phase, the overflow group performed simultaneous maximal isometric contraction of the hip flexors at 70% MVIC, while both groups performed handgrip strength tests. The outcomes were analyzed using multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA), with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.
Trial.results_ipd_description: The data collected in this study, including non-identified individual participant data (such as handgrip strength measurements and demographic information), will be shared for research purposes. The shared data will include detailed information on baseline characteristics, force measurements, and statistical analyses. These data will be made available after the publication of the study results in a peer-reviewed journal. The data will be accessible for a period of 5 years. Access will be granted to researchers who can demonstrate a legitimate need to use the data for further scientific analysis, and requests should be made through the corresponding author. The study protocol and statistical analysis plan will also be available upon request.

Trial.Public_title: The impact of differences in femoral implant design on the peri-implant bone mineral density, muscle strength, and activity level in total hip replacement surgery
Trial.Scientific_title: The impact of differences in femoral implant design on the peri-implant bone mineral density, muscle strength, and activity level in total hip replacement surgery - EU-SCT1
Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Ehime University Graduate School of Medicine Department of Orthopaedic Surgery
Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria:
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: 1) Patients unable to achieve outdoor ambulation, even with the assistance of walking aids (e.g., canes, walkers). 2) Patients with cognitive impairment precluding informed consent, or those otherwise unable to express intention to participate; additionally, any patient deemed unsuitable for study inclusion by the principal investigator or sub-investigators. 3) Patients diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the hip secondary to infection or trauma, idiopathic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), or high-grade developmental dysplasia of the hip (Crowe type III or IV). 4) Patients assessed by the attending physician, based on pre-operative CT planning, as having poor suitability for femoral implant fixation due to anatomical or bone quality concerns.
Trial.Intervention:
The Insignia Stem utilizes a tapered wedge geometry for fixation within the proximal femur. A key design feature is its substantial proximal volume aimed at maximizing metaphyseal fill in lateral view. The stem incorporates a full hydroxyapatite (HA) coating.
The Accolade 2 Stem utilizes a tapered wedge geometry for fixation within the proximal femur. A key design feature is its flat shape in lateral view. The stem incorporates a 3D porous coating in proximal part.
Trial.Primary_outcome: The primary outcome is the change in periprosthetic bone mineral density, measured quantitatively at 1, 2, and 5 years postoperatively using bone mineral density testing around the stem. This change will be calculated relative to the bone mineral density around the stem measured on the 7th day after THA surgery, and the effect of differences in stem design on these changes in periprosthetic bone mineral density will be compared between the two groups.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: Secondary outcomes will compare the two groups regarding the impact of stem design differences on radiological evaluations (plain radiographs and CT scans) and on pre- and post-operative clinical evaluations, including muscle strength, patient-reported outcomes, activity level, and other relevant factors.

Trial.Exclusion_Criteria:

Trial.Intervention:
This is a 2 x 2 nested factorial RCT where participants will be randomized to a training intervention (higher or lower load) and then randomized within each arm to receive either whey or casein protein.

They will perform 10 weeks of resistance exercise training (training twice weekly) and be given 40 g of whey or casein protein (also by random assignment) following each training session. Trial.Primary_sponsor: Universidade Federal dos Vales do Jequitinhonha e Mucuri

Trial.Contact_Affiliation: Universidade Federal dos Vales do Jequitinhonha e Mucuri

Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Cardiovascular, respiratory, osteoarticular diseases; use of medications; smoking
Trial.Intervention: This is a randomized, crossover study with two arms in which the subjects will be their own controls. A total of 20 adult individuals (men and women) who meet the eligibility criteria will participate in the study. The study will be randomized and crossover, that is, the individuals will be their own controls. During the results analysis phase, the researchers who will evaluate the outcomes will not be aware of the experimental situation. The participants will undergo an anamnesis, anthropometric analyses to measure height, body mass, waist circumference and body composition, will answer the morning-evening questionnaire to assess the chronotype (Horne JA et al. 1976), a familiarization period and the strength assessment. Then, we will use the protocol by Silva R. et al, 2023, of 4 experimental sessions, randomized, separated by at least 4 days, with two of these sessions carried out with strength exercises: session 1: resistance exercise protocol completed 3 hours before the usual bedtime; Session 2: resistance exercise protocol completed 1 hour before the usual bedtime; Session 3: without exercises 3 hours before the usual bedtime (control); Session 4: without exercises 1 hour before the usual bedtime (control). In sessions 1 and 2, 7 exercises will be performed for the major muscle groups (1 - Squat with hexagonal bar; 2 - Bench press with bar; 3 - Horizontal leg press; 4 - Pull-up with bar; 5 - Leg extension; 6 - Shoulder development on the machine; 7 - Leg curl; Figure 1), totaling 21 sets. The sessions will be held at night, 4 and 2 hours before the participants bedtime, beginning and end of the night respectively, keeping the sleep diary and actigraphy record from the first session performed. Participants will be asked to complete a questionnaire based on the lat;I03.350
Trial.Primary_outcome: A statistically significant mean difference of at least 1 hour in total sleep time (time between the start and end of sleep) is expected

Trial.Inclusion_Criteria: Inclusion criteria: Individuals = 20 years and < 60 years; Not having a previous diagnosis of type 1 or type 2 DM; Displaying a body mass index (BMI) = 25 and = 34.9 kg/m², that is, overweight and grade 1 obesity; Having access to a WhatsApp application; Having access to the internet and a personal cell phone; Having a diagnosis of pre-diabetes or gestational diabetes (past) or a score equal to or greater than five in the Diabetes Risk Screening proposed by the American Diabetes Association – ADA
Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Pregnant women; People with diabetes mellitus, of any type; Unable to practice physical activity, as per medical advice; People with serious neurological or psychiatric problems; People with neoplasms, chronic transmissible diseases, liver or kidney failure, untreated thyroid dysfunction, congestive heart failure and coronary artery disease; Use of anti-obesity medication and/or oral antidiabetic medication; protein supplementation and use of hormone therapy; Have participated in a concomitant weight control program or a medically prescribed diet; Have undergone bariatric surgery in the last three years, or are planning to undergo surgery in the next 12 months
Trial.Intervention: This is a randomized, controlled, single-blind clinical study for participants. Experimental group: 25 adults, of both sexes, who are overweight or obese and have some associated risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus will receive an individualized eating plan, specific nutritional guidelines for diabetes prevention and will participate in a multidisciplinary educational intervention, with a nutritionist, physical educator and psychologist, whose methodology will be an adaptation of the curriculum of the North American Diabetes Prevention Program, called PreventT2 (A Proven Program to Prevent or Delay Type 2 Diabetes). Control group: 25 adults who are overweight or obese, of both sexes, and have some associated risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus will receive an individualized eating plan and general nutritional guidelines for diabetes prevention. Allocation into groups was done randomly. The multidisciplinary educational intervention will involve participation in five in-person and remote meetings, where topics relevant to diabetes prevention will be addressed, namely: Healthy Eating, Physical Activity and Motivation. The meetings will last 90 minutes each, with weekly frequency.;E02.642.249.200;G11.427.410.698.277;F01.145.113.547
Trial.Primary_outcome: A weight loss of 5% in relation to the current weight is expected, using the weight assessment at baseline and after the intervention. The participant is asked to appear on the day wearing light clothing, such as a t-shirt and gym shorts. Weight measurements are made according to the original technique recommended by LOHMAN (1988), assessed twice by the same researcher, with the measurement recorded in kg.;A reduction in glycated hemoglobin is expected by measuring fasting HbA1c before and after the intervention. Blood samples will be collected by a legally qualified professional, through a 20 mL aliquot of the cubital vein (estimated duration of 5 minutes/person), always early in the morning, after a period of 8 to 12 hours of fasting, on the same day as the scheduled nutritional consultations.;It is expected that the population will experience an increase in the consumption of minimally processed foods and a reduction in ultra-processed foods, using the qualitative food frequency questionnaire method adapted from FURLAN-VIEBIG; PASTOR-VALERO (2004), which includes some regional foods from the state of Pernambuco. Consumption will be assessed based on the frequency of daily consumption of the food groups, before and after the intervention.;It is expected to achieve an increase in the weekly time dedicated to physical activity by collecting information using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), in its short version (MATSUDO et al., 2012). The questionnaire includes questions related to the time spent walking, moderate and vigorous activity in the week prior to the interview, including activities carried out at work, transportation, leisure, sports or domestic activities.
Trial.Secondary_outcome: No secondary outcomes are expected
Trial.Source_Support: Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico
Trial.results_ipd_description: Individual data of de-identified participants (including dictionaries and databases) will not be shared. Only the study protocol of the multidisciplinary educational intervention developed for the RCT will be available for consultation, along with the Guide for participants and professionals translated and adapted from the original American version, for two years after the end of the study, which is scheduled for the second half of 2026. These data may be shared with researchers interested in developing similar educational interventions for diabetes prevention.

Trial.Exclusion_Criteria: Exclusion criteria: Inpatients from pediatric, psychiatric, intensive care and neurosurgical wards as well as those from intermediate care were excluded, because of their different nutritional needs in comparison to somatically ill patients in routine care. We also excluded inpatients who were in more than one intervention phase.
Trial.Intervention:
Group 1: Baseline Cohort: Patients received the standard menu plan without any intervention.
Group 2: Cohort 2: Order Nudge - patients received a menu plan on which the plant-based menu was listed first.
Group 3: Cohort 3: Order - Recommendation Nudge - patients received a menu plan on which the plant-based menu was listed first. In addition, the plant-based menu was presented as the "kitchens recommendation of the day" by the menu assistants.
Trial.Primary_outcome: Number of plant-based menus selected
Trial.Secondary_outcome: Predictive value of age, sex and days in the intervention on the number of plant-based menus selected.
Trial.Source_Support: Karl und Veronica Carstens-Stiftung;Rut- u. Klaus-Bahlsen-Stiftung
Trial.results_summary: This study investigated the effectiveness of different nudging strategies on choosing plant-based meals in adult hospital inpatients as part of a healthier and more sustainable diet. Although absolute changes in selection rates were modest, our findings suggest that nudging can be a simply to implement and effective strategy towards healthier, more sustainable dietary choices in hospital inpatients, benefiting both the individual and the planet. Future research should investigate the differential effectiveness of different nudges, preferably in controlled settings.
